bug_description.normalized: The NCP Spinel property `SPINEL_PROP_MESHCOP_COMMISSIONER_GENERATE_PSKC` parses a passphrase string, a network-name string, and an 8-byte Extended PAN ID from the attacker-controlled UART frame and forwards them into `Commissioner::GeneratePskc()`. That function builds a PBKDF2 salt in a fixed 30-byte stack buffer sized for `"Thread"` (6 bytes), the Extended PAN ID (8 bytes), and a legal 16-byte Thread network name. The vulnerable code validates only the passphrase length, not the network-name length. The staged witness supplies a 17-byte network name, so `memcpy(salt + 14, aNetworkName, 17)` overruns the stack `salt` buffer by one byte and AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 17.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled Spinel payload after HDLC and Spinel header admission. It materializes the command value that decides whether the frame will be handled as a property update.
source.value_from: After HDLC decoding strips the outer `0x7e` flags and the trailing two bytes as FCS, the inner Spinel frame begins `8f 03 87 30 ...`. This read consumes byte `03` and yields `SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_SET`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This second UTF-8 field in the property payload becomes the network-name pointer later measured by `strlen(aNetworkName)` and copied into the fixed-size stack salt buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the staged witness, the bytes after the passphrase terminator are `0x20` repeated 17 times followed by `0x00`, so this call materializes a 17-byte network name consisting of spaces.
tainted_value_origin.note: `SpinelDecoder::ReadUtf8()` only requires a NUL terminator before the end of the remaining frame; it does not enforce `OT_NETWORK_NAME_MAX_SIZE`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The network-name copy starts 14 bytes into the 30-byte stack `salt` buffer and uses the attacker-controlled string length as its write size.

root_cause.description: Missing upper-bound validation for the network-name argument before assembling the fixed-size PBKDF2 salt.

parser_admitted.description: The HDLC decoder has already produced the inner Spinel frame and stripped the final two bytes as FCS before this call. `HandleReceive()` accepted header `0x8f` as a Spinel frame, so line 354 begins command parsing on the attacker-controlled payload.

coarse_trace.summary: The decoded Spinel frame is parsed as `SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_SET`, then the packed property key is read as `SPINEL_PROP_MESHCOP_COMMISSIONER_GENERATE_PSKC` to select the PSKC setter path.
The property handler materializes the passphrase string, the oversized network-name string, and an 8-byte Extended PAN ID directly from the Spinel payload, then forwards them into PSKC generation.
PSKC generation allocates a fixed 30-byte stack salt buffer and validates only the passphrase length before copying the constant prefix and the 8-byte Extended PAN ID.

With `saltLen` advanced to 14, the function uses `strlen(aNetworkName)` as the next copy size. The witness supplies length 17, so the network-name memcpy overruns the 16-byte tail of `salt` and matches the ASan stack-buffer-overflow write.

fine_trace.note: This is the first project-side read of the attacker-controlled Spinel payload after header admission. In the staged witness, the next byte is `0x03`, so `ReadUintPacked()` yields `command == SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_SET` and enters the property-update parser.
The property-update parser reads the next packed integer from bytes `87 30`, decoding `propKey == 0x1807`, which is `SPINEL_PROP_MESHCOP_COMMISSIONER_GENERATE_PSKC`.
The special-property switch matches `aKey == SPINEL_PROP_MESHCOP_COMMISSIONER_GENERATE_PSKC` and dispatches into the commissioner PSKC setter. Other property keys do not reach `GeneratePskc()`.

The first UTF-8 field is returned as a pointer into the Spinel frame and the decoder advances past its NUL terminator. In the witness this string is exactly six `0xff` bytes followed by `0x00`, so later `strlen(aPassPhrase)` is 6 and satisfies the minimum passphrase requirement.

The second UTF-8 parse returns the next NUL-terminated field from the same frame. In the witness this is 17 space bytes followed by `0x00`, so the overflow-driving `strlen(networkName)` will later be 17. `ReadUtf8()` requires only an in-frame terminator and does not apply the Thread network-name maximum.

fine_trace.code:
SuccessOrExit(error = mDecoder.ReadDataWithLen(extPanIdData, length));
VerifyOrExit(length == sizeof(spinel_net_xpanid_t), error = OT_ERROR_PARSE);
fine_trace.note: The final field is read as a little-endian length-prefixed blob. The witness bytes `08 00` set `length` to 8, the following eight `0x20` bytes become `extPanIdData`, and the handler accepts the PAN ID because the length matches `sizeof(spinel_net_xpanid_t)`.
The handler forwards the parsed passphrase pointer, network-name pointer, and 8-byte Extended PAN ID directly into PSKC generation. No local check constrains the network-name length before this call.

PSKC generation assembles its salt in a fixed 30-byte stack array. `OT_PBKDF2_SALT_MAX_LEN` is 30 because the intended layout is `"Thread"` (6) + Extended PAN ID (8) + a legal Thread network name of at most 16 bytes.

The only pre-copy size guard validates the passphrase. For the witness, `strlen(aPassPhrase) == 6`, so execution continues. There is no corresponding `strlen(aNetworkName) <= OT_NETWORK_NAME_MAX_SIZE` check here, even though the fix adds exactly that missing obligation at this site.
The constant prefix `"Thread"` is copied first, advancing `saltLen` from 0 to 6.

fine_trace.code:
memcpy(salt + saltLen, aExtPanId.m8, sizeof(aExtPanId));
saltLen += OT_EXT_PAN_ID_SIZE;
fine_trace.note: The 8-byte Extended PAN ID is appended next. `saltLen` advances from 6 to 14, leaving only 16 bytes of the 30-byte `salt` buffer available for the network name.

At the copy site, `strlen(aNetworkName)` evaluates to 17 from the witness's 17-space string, but steps 8-11 leave only `30 - 14 = 16` bytes remaining in `salt` at `salt + saltLen`. The requested copy size therefore exceeds the remaining destination extent by 1 byte.

The `memcpy` writes 17 bytes starting at `salt + 14`, overrunning the 30-byte stack array by one byte. The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 17` at `commissioner.cpp:1121` and identifies `salt` at line 1107 as the overflowed stack object.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix adds `strlen(aNetworkName) <= OT_NETWORK_NAME_MAX_SIZE` to the `VerifyOrExit` at lines 1110-1112, preventing the overflowing `memcpy(salt + saltLen, aNetworkName, strlen(aNetworkName))` call for the 17-byte witness network name.

format.name: HDLC-framed Spinel commissioner-generate-pskc request
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 43-byte witness staged in `poc`: `7e` start flag, then the Spinel frame bytes `8f 03 87 30 ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 08 00 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`, then two trailing `0x20` bytes that the HDLC decoder strips as FCS, then the closing `7e` flag. After HDLC decoding, the Spinel payload is a `SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_SET` for `SPINEL_PROP_MESHCOP_COMMISSIONER_GENERATE_PSKC` carrying a NUL-terminated 6-byte passphrase, a NUL-terminated 17-byte network name, and an 8-byte Extended PAN ID. That exact field layout makes `ReadUtf8(passPhrase)`, `ReadUtf8(networkName)`, and `ReadDataWithLen(extPanIdData, length)` succeed, passes the passphrase-only guard in `GeneratePskc()`, and drives `strlen(aNetworkName) == 17` at the overflowing copy into the 30-byte stack salt buffer.
